Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 25 May 2010 SB Member HALMAN H. ABUBAKAR Municipality of Jolo Province of Sulu Dear SB Member Abubakar: 56 s. 2010 This has reference to your query sent by facsimile on 24 May 2004 wherein you sought opinion from this Department pertaining to the possibility of proclaiming two (2) more winning candidates to the position of a Sanggunian Bayan on the basis of the claimed recent upgrade of the status of the Municipality of Jolo, Sulu from a '3rd Class' to a '1st Class Municipality' in the year 2009. Your query stemmed from the fact that the Commission on Elections had already proclaimed the winning candidates in the Municipality of Sulu from the Office of the Mayor, Vice Mayor and eight (8) members of the Sangguniang Bayan. The point of interest raised was to adopt a similar move done by the Provincial Government of Sulu which increased the number of its Provincial Board Menibers from four (4) to five (5) in view of the upgrade of in status from a 3rd Class Province to a 2nd Class. We reply in the NEGATIVE. It is the view of this Department that the Sangguniang Bayan of Sulu, Jolo is not entitled to any additional elective membership despite the upgrade in status. We invite your attention to the pertinent provision of Art. 94(c)(3), Rule XVII of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991, which explicitly states: "ART. 94. Manner of Election and Number of Elective Sangguniang Members. - xxx (c) SANGGUNIANG BAYAN - xxx (2) The number of election and elective members of the sangguninng bayan of the municipalities in the MMA shall be governed by the provisions of Section 2 of R.A. 6636, as amended, xxx. (3)All Otller municipalities shall have EIGHT MEMBERS to be elected at large by the qualified voters therein. x x. " (entphasis and underscoring supplied)

The law and the rules are clear. Under Republic Act No. 66361 the allotment of elective members to provinces and municipalities must be made on the basis of its classification as a province and/or municipality. (Herrera, et.al. vs COMELEC, G.R. No. 131499, 17 November 1999). Section 4 of the same law, particularly the second statement provides that "All other municipalities shall have the same number of elective members as provided in existing laws. The present state of law governing the subject query is cited herein, and we reiterate that the Sangguniang Bayan of municipalities other than those situated in the Metro Manila Area shall have EIGHT (8) MEMBERS elected at large by the qualified voters therein. Thank you very much and we hope that the foregoing suffices your concerns. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A . JESU Director III cc: DOQU IV HON. HAROUN ALRASHID A. LUCMAN, JR.
